name: Robert Tresilian
role: Chief Justice of the King's Bench
description: Appointed Chief Justice shortly after the revolt and given a special commission, alongside Thomas of Woodstock, on 20 June 1381 to try captured rebels. Conducted mass trials at Chelmsford (Essex) -- some accounts record roughly thirty executions there -- and traveled on to St Albans for further trials, including that of William Grindecobbe; later historians have criticized the proceedings' use of coercive or legally dubious methods to secure convictions.
narrative_function: The legal instrument of the post-revolt reckoning.
